```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "png",
                      dpi = 300,
                      cache = FALSE)
```

**This code offers an analysis of the 2018 blueberry study lead by Marta & Heather. The results are meant to assist with completion of the paper led by Amanda Gregoris.** 

**First, let's plot & analyze EFB incidence over time at each of the 4 "blueberry-only" yards (i.e. BC-1, BC-2, BC-3, and AB-2). As noted by Carolyn Taylor (UBC statistial consultant), each yard must be analyzed separately.** 

**Note that the "WF" (for "wild forage") group has been renamed the "non-BB" (for "non-blueberry") group, since some other agricultural crops still occur within the foraging range. In addition, most of the figures in the final version of the manuscript have been composed from these raw versions, where manipulations may include stitching panels and/or updating axis labels or aesthetics.** 

```{r}
#Relevant libraries will be loaded at the start of each code chunk
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(library(readxl)))
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(library(plyr)))
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(library(ggplot2)))

#Read in the EFB incidence data
EFB.PP.dat <- read_excel("Data summary_updated.xlsx", sheet = "EFB data T1-T3")
EFB.PP.dat$Colony <- as.character(EFB.PP.dat$Colony)
unique(EFB.PP.dat$Site.ID)
head(EFB.PP.dat)

```

```{r EFB-incidence-plot, fig.height = 2.5, fig.width = 6}

#Convert binary response (EFB y/n) to percents
EFB.inc.noNA <- EFB.PP.dat[EFB.PP.dat$EFB.incidence != "NA",]
EFB.inc.noNA$EFB.incidence <- as.numeric(EFB.inc.noNA$EFB.incidence)
EFB.inc.noNA$Time.point <- as.character(EFB.inc.noNA$Time.point)

agg.EFB.inc <- ddply(EFB.inc.noNA, c("Site.ID", "Time.point"), summarise,
                        EFB.percent = 100*sum(EFB.incidence)/length(EFB.incidence))

agg.EFB.sample <- ddply(EFB.inc.noNA, c("Site.ID", "Time.point"), summarise,
                        EFB.percent = 100*sum(EFB.incidence)/length(EFB.incidence),
                        N = length(EFB.incidence))

#Define levels for graphing
agg.EFB.inc$Site.ID <- factor(agg.EFB.inc$Site.ID, levels = c("WF AB-1", "BB AB-1", "BC-1", "BC-2", "BC-3", "AB-2"))
                              
ggplot(agg.EFB.inc, aes(x = Time.point, y = EFB.percent)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "navy") +
    scale_y_continuous(name = "EFB incidence (% symptomatic colonies)") +
    scale_x_discrete(name = "Time point")+
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.key.size = unit(.3, 'cm'),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
         plot.background = element_blank()) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~Site.ID, ncol = 6)
  
```
**Can we build a glm with time as a fixed effect, including all blueberry fields, with colony as a random effect nested within field?**

```{r}
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(library(lme4)))
BB.inc <- EFB.inc.noNA[EFB.inc.noNA$Forage == "BB",]
BB.inc$Time.point <- as.numeric(BB.inc$Time.point)
fit <- glmer(EFB.incidence ~ Time.point + (1|Site.ID/Colony), family = "binomial", data = BB.inc)
#simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = fit, plot = T) #good
summary(fit)

```
**Yes, we can fit this model and there is a significant effect of time on EFB incidence. However, since we cannot analyze the wildflower yard data this way, we will stick with the McNemar-Bowker test as suggested by Carolyn Taylor.**

**Conduct the McNemar-Bowker test (at each site separately)**

```{r}
MB.dat <- read_excel("Data summary_updated.xlsx", sheet = "EFB for MB test T1-T3")

#WF AB-1 yard - TP1-TP2
MB.WF1 <- MB.dat[MB.dat$Site.ID == "WF AB-1",]
table(MB.WF1$EFB.TP1, MB.WF1$EFB.TP2)
WF1.table1 <- as.table(rbind(c(43, 1), c(0,0))) #Need to encode manually when bottom row is made up of zeros
dimnames(WF1.table1) <- list(TP1 = c("No", "Yes"), TP2 = c("No", "Yes")) 
mcnemar.test(WF1.table1)

#WF AB-1 yard - TP2-TP3
WF1.table2 <- table(MB.WF1$EFB.TP2, MB.WF1$EFB.TP3)
WF1.table2
mcnemar.test(WF1.table2)

#WF AB-1 yard - TP1-TP3
table(MB.WF1$EFB.TP1, MB.WF1$EFB.TP3)
WF1.table3 <- as.table(rbind(c(29, 10), c(0,0)))
```

**Great. Now let's move on to comparing sites at time point 3, first plotting the data. Note that the EFB intensity data should exclude colonies without EFB symptoms, as the high frequency of zeroes will not be suitable for some of the downstream analyses.**


```{r EFB-incidence-tp3-Aggassiz, fig.height = 2.25, fig.width = 1.2}
#First plot the TP3 WF vs. BB data, including disease intensity
TP3.WF.BB <- EFB.inc.noNA[EFB.inc.noNA$Time.point == "3" & EFB.inc.noNA$Site == "Aggassiz",]
TP3.WF.BB$EFB.score <- as.numeric(TP3.WF.BB$EFB.score)

#Summarize the data
agg.TP3.WF.BB <- ddply(TP3.WF.BB, c("Site.ID"), summarise,
                       EFB.percent = 100*sum(EFB.incidence)/length(EFB.incidence))
agg.TP3.WF.BB$Site.ID <- c("BB", "WF")
agg.TP3.WF.BB$Site.ID <-  factor(agg.TP3.WF.BB$Site.ID, levels = c("WF", "BB"))

ggplot(agg.TP3.WF.BB, aes(x = Site.ID, y = EFB.percent)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "navy") +
    scale_y_continuous(name = "EFB incidence (% symptomatic colonies)", limits = c(0,60)) +
    scale_x_discrete(name = "Yard")+
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.key.size = unit(.3, 'cm'),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
         plot.background = element_blank()) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank())

```

**Now let's conduct the statistics, starting with Fisher Exact test on TP3 incidence data**

```{r}
suppressMessages(suppressWarnings(library(tibble)))

#Make contingency table for WF vs BB
agg.TP3.WF.BB <- ddply(TP3.WF.BB, c("Site.ID"), summarise,
                        EFB.yes = sum(EFB.incidence),
                        EFB.no = length(EFB.incidence)-sum(EFB.incidence))
agg.TP3.WF.BB #take a look
agg.TP3.WF.BB <- column_to_rownames(agg.TP3.WF.BB, var = "Site.ID") #Format rownames

fisher.test(agg.TP3.WF.BB)


#Make contingency table for others
agg.TP3.other <- ddply(TP3.other, c("Site.ID"), summarise,
                        EFB.yes = sum(EFB.incidence),
                        EFB.no = length(EFB.incidence)-sum(EFB.incidence))
agg.TP3.other #take a look
agg.TP3.other <- column_to_rownames(agg.TP3.other, var = "Site.ID") #Format rownames

fisher.test(agg.TP3.other)

#conduct posthoc testing on each pairwise comparison
Fisher.AB2.BC1 <- agg.TP3.other[rownames(agg.TP3.other) %in% c("AB-2", "BC-1"),]
fisher.test(Fisher.AB2.BC1)

Fisher.AB2.BC2 <- agg.TP3.other[rownames(agg.TP3.other) %in% c("AB-2", "BC-2"),]
fisher.test(Fisher.AB2.BC2)

Fisher.AB2.BC3 <- agg.TP3.other[rownames(agg.TP3.other) %in% c("AB-2", "BC-3"),]
fisher.test(Fisher.AB2.BC3)

Fisher.BC1.BC2 <- agg.TP3.other[rownames(agg.TP3.other) %in% c("BC-1", "BC-2"),]
fisher.test(Fisher.BC1.BC2)

Fisher.BC1.BC3 <- agg.TP3.other[rownames(agg.TP3.other) %in% c("BC-1", "BC-3"),]
fisher.test(Fisher.BC1.BC3)

Fisher.BC2.BC3 <- agg.TP3.other[rownames(agg.TP3.other) %in% c("BC-2", "BC-3"),]
fisher.test(Fisher.BC2.BC3)
```

**Only one of the above comparisons was significant after Bonferroni correction (BC-1 & BC-2). Now let's conduct statistics on EFB intensity data**

```{r}
library(dunn.test)
kruskal.test(EFB.score ~ Forage, data = TP3.WF.BB.inten) 

kruskal.test(EFB.score ~ Site.ID, data = TP3.other.inten)
dunn.test(TP3.other.inten$EFB.score, TP3.other.inten$Site.ID, method = "Bonferroni")

```

**Moving on to visualize population sizes**

```{r adult.frames, fig.height = 2.5, fig.width = 4.5}
pop.dat <- read_excel("Data summary_updated.xlsx", sheet = "Population data T1-T2")
pop.dat.noNA <- pop.dat[pop.dat$Adult != "NA",]
pop.dat.noNA$Adult <- as.numeric(pop.dat.noNA$Adult)
pop.dat.noNA$Brood <- as.numeric(pop.dat.noNA$Brood)
pop.dat.noNA$Colony <- as.character(pop.dat.noNA$Colony)

pop.dat.noNA$Adult.frames <- pop.dat.noNA$Adult/2
pop.dat.noNA$Brood.frames <- pop.dat.noNA$Brood/2

agg.pop.dat <- ddply(pop.dat.noNA, c("Site.ID", "Time.point"), summarise,
                        adult.mean = mean(Adult.frames),
                        adult.sd = sd(Adult.frames),
                        brood.mean = mean(Brood.frames),
                        brood.sd = sd(Brood.frames))


agg.pop.dat$Site.ID <- factor(agg.pop.dat$Site.ID, levels = c("WF AB-1", "BB AB-1", "BC-1", "BC-2", "BC-3", "AB-2"))
agg.pop.dat$Time.point <- as.character(agg.pop.dat$Time.point)

ggplot(agg.pop.dat, aes(x = Time.point, y = adult.mean)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", fill = "navy") +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=adult.mean, ymax=adult.mean+adult.sd), width=.2)+
    scale_y_continuous(name = "Frames of adult bees") +
    scale_x_discrete(name = "Time point")+
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.key.size = unit(.3, 'cm'),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),

        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),

        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
         plot.background = element_blank()) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~Site.ID, ncol = 6)
```

What happens when we include varroa as a predictor?

```{r}
varroa.dat <- read_excel("Data summary_updated.xlsx", sheet = "Varroa data")
varroa.dat$combo <- paste(varroa.dat$Colony, varroa.dat$Time.point, sep = ".")

pop.dat.noNA$combo <- paste(pop.dat.noNA$Colony, pop.dat.noNA$Time.point, sep = ".")
pop.combo <-pop.dat.noNA[pop.dat.noNA$combo %in% varroa.dat$combo,]
varroa.dat <- varroa.dat[varroa.dat$combo %in% pop.combo$combo,]
varroa.dat <- varroa.dat[order(varroa.dat$combo),]
pop.combo <- pop.combo[order(pop.combo$combo),]
varroa.dat$combo == pop.combo$combo
pop.combo$varroa <- varroa.dat$Mite.percent

pop.combo$EFB <- factor(pop.combo$EFB, levels = c("0", "1"))
fit <- lmer(Brood.frames ~ Time.point + varroa + EFB+ (1|Site.ID/Colony), data = pop.combo)
summary(fit)
```

What about using ddPCR instead of EFB?

```{r}
ddPCR <- read_excel("Data summary_updated.xlsx", sheet = "ddPCR")
ddPCR$combo <- paste(ddPCR$Colony, ddPCR$Time.point, sep = ".")
ddPCR.slim <- ddPCR[ddPCR$combo %in% pop.combo$combo,]
ddPCR.slim <- ddPCR.slim[order(ddPCR.slim$combo),]
ddPCR.slim$combo == pop.combo$combo
pop.combo$ddPCR <- ddPCR.slim$EFB.ddPCR

pop.combo.slim <- pop.combo[!is.na(pop.combo$ddPCR),]
fit <- lmer(Brood.frames ~ Time.point + varroa + ddPCR + (1|Site.ID/Colony), data = pop.combo)
summary(fit)

```

**First conduct PP statistics on the Aggassiz yards (WF & BB) for EFB incidence**


**Now let's do some statistics on each time point separately. I will use the Mann-Whitney U test and Bonferroni correction because comparing medians is most appropriate for varroa data, which contains lots of zeroes.**

```{r}
AB1.TP1 <- var[var$Site == "Aggassiz" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Forage, data = AB1.TP1, exact = FALSE)

AB1.TP2 <- var[var$Site == "Aggassiz" & var$Time.point == "2",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Forage, data = AB1.TP2, exact = FALSE)

BC1.BC2.TP1 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-1" | var$Site.ID == "BC-2" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC1.BC2.TP1, exact = FALSE)

BC1.BC2.TP2 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-1" | var$Site.ID == "BC-2" & var$Time.point == "2",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC1.BC2.TP2, exact = FALSE)

BC1.BC3.TP1 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-1" | var$Site.ID == "BC-3" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC1.BC3.TP1, exact = FALSE)

BC1.BC3.TP2 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-1" | var$Site.ID == "BC-3" & var$Time.point == "2",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC1.BC3.TP2, exact = FALSE)

BC1.AB2.TP1 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-1" | var$Site.ID == "AB-2" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC1.AB2.TP1, exact = FALSE)

BC1.AB2.TP2 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-1" | var$Site.ID == "AB-2" & var$Time.point == "2",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC1.AB2.TP2, exact = FALSE)

BC2.BC3.TP1 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-2" | var$Site.ID == "BC-3" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC2.BC3.TP1, exact = FALSE)

BC2.BC3.TP2 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-2" | var$Site.ID == "BC-3" & var$Time.point == "2",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC2.BC3.TP2, exact = FALSE)

BC2.AB2.TP1 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-2" | var$Site.ID == "AB-2" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC2.AB2.TP1, exact = FALSE)

BC2.AB2.TP2 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-2" | var$Site.ID == "AB-2" & var$Time.point == "2",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC2.AB2.TP2, exact = FALSE)

BC3.AB2.TP1 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-3" | var$Site.ID == "AB-2" & var$Time.point == "1",]
wilcox.test(Mite.percent ~ Site.ID, data = BC3.AB2.TP1, exact = FALSE)

BC3.AB2.TP2 <- var[var$Site.ID == "BC-3" | var$Site.ID == "AB-2" & var$Time.point == "2",]
```

**Now let's analyze the ddPCR data for EFB abundance in adult bees sampled from the colonies.**


```{r efb-ratio-by-incidence, fig.height = 2, fig.width = 2.5}
#Read in ddPCR data
pcr <- read_excel("Data summary_updated.xlsx", sheet = "EFB data T1-T3")
pcr$field.incidence <- as.character(pcr$EFB.incidence)

pcr <- pcr[!is.na(pcr$EFB.incidence),]
pcr$field.incidence[pcr$field.incidence == "0"] <- "Asymptomatic"
pcr$field.incidence[pcr$field.incidence == "1"] <- "Symptomatic"
pcr$pcr.detect <- pcr$EFB.ddPCR
pcr$pcr.detect[pcr$pcr.detect > 0] <- 1
pcr$pcr.detect[pcr$pcr.detect == 0] <- 0

pcr$log.PCR <- log2(pcr$EFB.ddPCR)
agg <- ddply(pcr, c("field.incidence", "Time.point"), summarise,
                       EFB.pcr = mean(EFB.ddPCR, na.rm = TRUE),
                        EFB.log = mean(log.PCR, na.rm=TRUE),
                        EFB.sd = sd(EFB.ddPCR, na.rm = TRUE),
                        EFB.log.sd = sd(log.PCR, na.rm=TRUE),
                        count = length(EFB.ddPCR))
sum(agg$count)

agg$Time.point <- factor(agg$Time.point, levels = c("1","2","3"))
pcr <- data.frame(pcr)
ggplot(agg, aes(x = Time.point, y = EFB.pcr)) +
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(), color = "black", fill = c("navy","navy","navy","navy","navy","navy") ) +
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=EFB.pcr, ymax=EFB.pcr+EFB.sd),width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.9))+
   geom_jitter(data = pcr, aes(x=Time.point, y = EFB.ddPCR),
             width = 0.1, 
             size = .5, alpha = .5)+
    scale_y_continuous(name = "EFB ddPCR ratio") +
    scale_x_discrete(name = "Time point")+
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.key.size = unit(.3, 'cm'),
          panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank(),
        panel.background = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.title.x = element_text(size = 8),
        axis.text.y = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),
        axis.text.x = element_text(colour="black", size = 8),
        axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
         plot.background = element_blank()) +
  theme(strip.background = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~field.incidence)
```

```{r}
library(emmeans)
pcr <- pcr[!is.na(pcr$pcr.detect),]
pcr$Time.point <- as.character(pcr$Time.point)
wf <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "nonBB AB-1",]
fit <- glmer(pcr.detect ~ Time.point + (1|Colony), data = wf, family = "binomial")
summary(fit)
marginal = emmeans(fit, ~ Time.point)
pairs(marginal)

bb <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "BB AB-1",]
fit <- glmer(pcr.detect ~ Time.point + (1|Colony), data = bb, family = "binomial")
summary(fit)
marginal = emmeans(fit, ~ Time.point)
pairs(marginal)

bc1 <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "BC-1",]
fit <- glmer(pcr.detect ~ Time.point + (1|Colony), data = bc1, family = "binomial")
marginal = emmeans(fit, ~ Time.point)
pairs(marginal)
summary(fit)

bc2 <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "BC-2",]
fit <- glmer(pcr.detect ~ Time.point + (1|Colony), data = bc2, family = "binomial")
summary(fit)
marginal = emmeans(fit, ~ Time.point)
pairs(marginal)

bc3 <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "BC-3",]
fit <- glmer(pcr.detect ~ Time.point + (1|Colony), data = bc3, family = "binomial")
summary(fit)
marginal = emmeans(fit, ~ Time.point)
pairs(marginal)

ab2 <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "AB-2",]
fit <- glmer(pcr.detect ~ Time.point + (1|Colony), data = ab2, family = "binomial")
summary(fit)
marginal = emmeans(fit, ~ Time.point)
pairs(marginal)

ab1 <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID == "nonBB AB-1" | pcr$Site.ID == "BB AB-1",]
tp3.ab1 <- ab1[ab1$Time.point == 3,]
agg.ab1 <- ddply(tp3.ab1, c("Site.ID"), summarise,
                        PCR.yes = sum(pcr.detect),
                        PCR.no = length(pcr.detect)-sum(pcr.detect))
agg.ab1 <- column_to_rownames(agg.ab1, var = "Site.ID") #take a look
fisher.test(agg.ab1)

other <- pcr[pcr$Site.ID != "nonBB AB-1" & pcr$Site.ID != "BB AB-1" & pcr$Time.point == 3 & !is.na(pcr$pcr.detect),]

agg.other <- ddply(other, c("Site.ID"), summarise,
                        PCR.yes = sum(pcr.detect),
                        PCR.no = length(pcr.detect)-sum(pcr.detect))
agg.other <- column_to_rownames(agg.other, var = "Site.ID")
fisher.test(agg.other)
```
